lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach opposite leaves plus possible stipules/interpetiolar lines and a superior commonly 2-locular ovary, then use local Spigelia and Mitreola fruit architecture.

project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas family-first module centered on Spigelia hedyotidea and Mitreola petiolata
project_scope.note: Older broad Loganiaceae treatments may include Gelsemium; the current learner follows the modern split with Gelsemiaceae separate.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Check opposite leaves for stipules or an interpetiolar line, then inspect the fused 4–5-part corolla and a superior to semi-inferior usually 2-locular ovary. Local confirmation comes from capsule architecture.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Herbs to woody plants across the family; local project genera are herbs/subshrubs. Leaves usually opposite, simple and entire; stipules/interpetiolar lines may be obvious, reduced or absent.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually bisexual, 4–5-merous with a fused tubular/funnelform corolla; stamens attached to the corolla and alternating with its lobes. Ovary usually superior or semi-inferior, commonly 2-locular with axile placentation.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Capsules or berries across the family. Local Mitreola has a distinctive 2-horned, 2-valved capsule; Spigelia has a short capsule and the genus can open circumscissilely.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: For the local pool, fruit is king: two-horned Mitreola capsules or pinkroot-style Spigelia capsules make the family far easier than flowers alone.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: opposite node/stipule line → fused flower → superior 2-locular ovary → two local fruit doors → modern Gelsemium split
visual_lesson.intro: Loganiaceae is a good reminder that close relatives can share the same fused-flower gestalt. The local fruit shapes—especially Mitreola's horns—make the family memorable.

steps.title: 1 · Inspect the space between opposite petioles
steps.look_for: Stipules may be present as a small membrane, ridge or interpetiolar line, though they can also be reduced.
steps.why_it_matters: This contrasts with exstipulate Gentianaceae and sets up the Rubiaceae comparison.

steps.title: 2 · Spigelia door: paired leaves + terminal small cyme
steps.look_for: Low perennial herb with paired opposite leaves and a small terminal monochasial/2-flowered cyme of white flowers suffused with pink/yellow.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the most locally distinctive Loganiaceae flower pattern in the pool.

steps.title: 3 · Mitreola door: find the horned capsule
steps.look_for: Tiny 2-valved capsule ending in two obvious horns.
steps.why_it_matters: The two-horned fruit is one of the strongest genus-level characters in the entire batch.

steps.title: 4 · Compare ovary position with Rubiaceae
steps.look_for: Loganiaceae local genera have a superior ovary; Rubiaceae anchors place the ovary below the visible floral whorls.
steps.why_it_matters: This prevents opposite leaves + stipules from automatically becoming Rubiaceae.

steps.title: 5 · Keep Gelsemium out of the old broad family
steps.look_for: Older literature may call Gelsemium Loganiaceae; the current learner places it in Gelsemiaceae.

comparisons.title: Loganiaceae vs Gentianaceae
comparisons.rule: Loganiaceae may have stipules/interpetiolar lines and commonly has a 2-locular axile ovary; Gentianaceae is generally exstipulate and commonly has a 1-locular ovary with parietal placentation.

comparisons.title: Loganiaceae vs Rubiaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have opposite leaves and interpetiolar structures. Rubiaceae's ovary is inferior; local Loganiaceae has a superior ovary.

comparisons.title: Loganiaceae vs Gelsemiaceae
comparisons.rule: Gelsemium was historically included in broad Loganiaceae, but current classification separates Gelsemiaceae. The local Gelsemium door is a woody twining vine with yellow flowers and winged seeds, unlike the herbaceous Spigelia/Mitreola project pattern.

visual_lesson.caveat: Loganiaceae is morphologically diverse and stipules are not always obvious. Use ovary/fruit architecture with the node characters.

genera.fast_cue: opposite leaves + terminal monochasial small tubular/funnelform flowers + short capsule

visual_targets.annotation_goal: label horns, valves and seed cavity
